template: Public Forum debate is designed to be accessible to a general audience. {context} It focuses on current events and uses a more natural conversational tone than policy debate.

template: Informal debate is more like a structured conversation. {context} Unlike competitive formats, it often lacks a moderator and fixed time limits.

template: Oxford-style debates are unique because the audience votes before and after the debate. {context} The winner is determined by who shifted the most opinions.
fallback: Oxford-style debate focuses on whether the speakers can actually change the minds of the audience, measured by pre- and post-debate polling.
